lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 4: Adversarial Robustness and Generative Models

unit.name: High-dimensional vulnerability, FGSM, and defenses
unit.description: Explains adversarial vulnerability through high-dimensional compounding effects, introduces FGSM, and surveys defenses including sanitization, adversarial training, red teaming, and RLHF.
unit.summary: The instructor rejects the simple explanation that neural networks are vulnerable mainly because of nonlinearity and instead points to high dimensionality and approximately linear behavior from inputs to logits [ts=1680s]. A logistic-regression-style example shows that adding a small epsilon-scaled weight vector can produce a large shift in the sigmoid output because many small coordinate changes accumulate [ts=1796s]. This intuition leads to the Fast Gradient Sign Method, which makes a one-shot perturbation in the sign direction of the input gradient while keeping the image visually similar [ts=1915s]. The segment distinguishes white-box attackers with parameter access from black-box attackers without it [ts=2026s]. Defenses include input sanitization, output filtering, training on correctly labeled adversarial examples, adversarial training with an added adversarial-loss term, red teaming, and RLHF-style post-training [ts=2099s].

key_points.text: Neural-network vulnerability is attributed to high-dimensional compounding effects rather than just nonlinear activations.
For x* = x + epsilon w, the logit includes an epsilon times squared-weight term, so many small perturbations accumulate.
FGSM forms a one-shot adversarial example by adding epsilon times the sign of the loss gradient with respect to the input.
White-box attacks assume access to model parameters, while black-box attacks do not.
Adversarial training augments the loss with correctly labeled adversarial inputs, often generated by FGSM.

kp_catalog.name: High-dimensional compounding vulnerability
kp_catalog.description: Small input perturbations across many dimensions can accumulate into a large change in model output, especially when the network behaves approximately linearly from input to logits.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor uses a logistic-regression example to connect high dimensionality, near-linearity, and compounding perturbation effects [ts=1680s][ts=1818s].

kp_catalog.name: Fast Gradient Sign Method
kp_catalog.description: One-shot adversarial attack that perturbs each input dimension by a small epsilon in the sign direction of the loss gradient with respect to the input.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: FGSM is presented as the simple one-shot version of adversarial input optimization and is later reused for adversarial training [ts=1915s][ts=2264s].

kp_catalog.name: Adversarial defense strategies
kp_catalog.description: Defenses including safety nets, input sanitization, output filtering, adversarial training, red teaming, RLHF, and constitutional AI, none of which fully eliminates the attack-defense arms race.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor surveys defenses and stresses that attacks and defenses evolve together [ts=2041s][ts=2226s].
